claims.text: more than 50% of pediatric conjunctivitis is bacterial
claims.quote: Acute bacterial conjunctivitis is common in children, with more than 50% of conjunctivitis cases being bacterial in origin

claims.text: 2022 meta-analysis: up to 70% bacterial in children, about 16% in adults
claims.quote: with as many as 70% of conjunctivitis cases in children. The same meta-analysis found that adults presenting with acute conjunctivitis had an identified bacterial etiology much less often, only about 16% of the time.

claims.text: H. influenzae (most often non-typeable) most common, up to 70%; S. pneumoniae, M. catarrhalis common
claims.quote: Common pathogens include Haemophilus influenzae, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Moraxella catarrhalis. ... remains the most common cause of bacterial conjunctivitis, present in up to 70% of cases

claims.text: bacterial usually clears in 7 to 10 days without treatment
claims.quote: The vast majority of cases of bacterial conjunctivitis are self-limiting, lasting 7 to 10 days without treatment.

claims.text: one trial: 4.0 vs 3.8 days; 8% adverse reactions; acquired resistance in children
claims.quote: from a mean of 4.0 days with a placebo to a mean of 3.8 days with moxifloxacin treatment []. Antibiotics are not without risk, with adverse drug reactions reported by 8% of patients using ophthalmic antibiotics

claims.text: acquired resistance in conjunctival bacteria of children prescribed antibiotics; no difference in sight-threatening outcomes
claims.quote: studies have shown acquired resistance to pathogenic bacteria in the conjunctiva of children prescribed antibiotics ... no differences in sight threatening outcomes have been observed between treatment and non-treatment groups

claims.text: meta-analysis of 11 RCTs, 3,673 patients, 10% increase in clinical improvement
claims.quote: In a meta-analysis consisting of 11 randomized clinical trials and 3673 patients, there was a 10% increase in the rate of clinical improvement for patients who received early antibiotic treatment

claims.text: no treatment, delayed treatment, immediate treatment all appropriate
claims.quote: no treatment, a delayed treatment approach, and immediate treatment all are appropriate responses to suspected uncomplicated bacterial conjunctivitis

claims.text: Colorado study: drivers of the decision
claims.quote: the main drivers behind choosing to prescribe or withhold antibiotics were the patient’s clinical presentation, family expectations, antibiotic stewardship concerns, diagnostic uncertainty, and daycare and school policies

claims.text: families often say antibiotics are needed for return to school or daycare
claims.quote: In many cases, families will assert that treatment with antibiotics is necessary for their child to return to school or daycare

claims.text: AAP notes antibiotics should not be required for return to care
claims.quote: the American Academy of Pediatrics specifically notes that antibiotics should not be required for return to care

claims.text: start with erythromycin ointment or trimethoprim-polymyxin B drops; improvement in 1 to 2 days
claims.quote: If treatment is desired, initial treatment would begin with erythromycin ointment or trimethoprim-polymyxin B ophthalmic drops. Symptoms would be expected to improve within one to two days.

claims.text: antibiotics indicated on an individual basis
claims.quote: antibiotics are indicated on an individual basis for cases of bacterial conjunctivitis

claims.text: 2003 meta-analysis: no diagnostic usefulness of signs; adults with culture-positive bacterial conjunctivitis: 35% serous or no discharge
claims.quote: A multi-center study of adults with bacterial conjunctivitis demonstrated that the symptoms can widely vary. Of those patients with positive bacterial cultures, 65% had burning, 58% had itching, and 35% had serous or no discharge

claims.text: bacterial: yellow-green purulent discharge, mattered eyelids in morning, one or both eyes
claims.quote: significant mucopurulent discharge, frequently yellow to green in color. Patients with acute bacterial conjunctivitis often complain of eyes that are mattered and adhered in the morning

claims.text: viral: adenovirus, gritty, watery discharge, spreads to other eye within 24 to 48 h, prodrome, highly contagious

claims.text: adenoviral conjunctivitis highly contagious; symptomatic treatment with cool compresses and artificial tears

claims.text: 46% of 26 adults had adenovirus from hand swabs

claims.text: minimize contact with others for 10 to 14 days from symptom onset
